title: The Hopf fibration: linked circles filling space
hook: Every point of the 2-sphere lifts to a circle in the 3-sphere, and every two of those circles are linked.
alt: A ring of colored tubes, each a closed circle, wraps around a doughnut shape so that every circle threads through all the others, and the arrangement turns slowly. Engaged, it can be orbited and zoomed, and a clicked circle is labeled with its point on the sphere.
author: @villarceau

pointer.hint: Drag to orbit · right-drag to pan · scroll to zoom · click a circle
Drag to orbit · pinch to zoom · tap a circle

targets.note: One self-contained HTML file with three.js inlined, for a lecture room without a network.

presets.label: One latitude = one torus
presets.note: Fibers over the equator of S² fill out the projected Clifford torus.

presets.label: Two latitudes link
presets.note: The inner torus comes from latitude 45°. Every one of its circles links every circle of the outer torus.

presets.label: Near the pole
presets.note: Close to the north pole the fibers hug the unit circle, the fiber over the pole itself.

presets.label: Look down the axis
presets.note: From above, the fibers over the equator are circles that all pass through the unit circle: the selected one goes once around it.

presets.label: Back to the turning view
presets.note: The camera, the slow turn and the selection go back to how the piece starts.
